chunks: As for what Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated, from 'Ali ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
I heard him say: There is no ghusl upon the woman in nifas during travel.

Its proper meaning is that ghusl is not upon her when she is unable to use water, whether because it is unavailable, or because she needs it for another use, or out of fear of the cold. What is not intended is that ghusl is not upon her in every circumstance.

key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel, the state of being on a journey
key_terms.النُّفَسَاءِ: a woman in the state of postnatal bleeding
key_terms.لِتَعَذُّرِهِ: because it is unavailable or inaccessible
key_terms.مَخَافَةِ الْبَرْدِ: fear of harm due to cold

ai.seo_question: Does a woman in nifas have to perform ghusl while traveling if she cannot use water?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of ghusl for a woman in nifas while traveling. It clarifies that the negation of ghusl applies only when use of water is not possible due to unavailability, need, or fear of harm from cold, and does not mean that ghusl is waived absolutely in all situations.
